Iran responds positively to latest mediator proposal - report November US UMich prelim consumer sentiment 51.0 vs 48.0 expected Iran reviewing proposals to curb nuclear program - report BOJ's Ueda: Consumer prices now around 3% and expected to rise further into early next year Microsoft is reportedly winding down it's Oracle deal to wind down AI cloud capacity Fed's Daly: Jobs report is good news Trump chief of staff Susie Wiles to be replaced by Stephen Miller Trump: We are talking to Iran, we are doing very well with Iran Markets: Gold down $22 to $4065 US 10-year yields down 2.4 bps to 4.86% WTI crude oil flat at $90.50 S&P 500 up 0.3% USD leads, AUD lags There was some good news after the close with OpenAI closing a funding round of $11 billion at a valuation of $1.25 trillion. The FT also reported that Anthropic continues to plan its IPO for this month and will raise $80-100 billion at a $1.25-1.75 trillion valuation. That should help things out next week, provided no other surprises. As for trading on Friday, non-farm payrolls helped to lift the dollar as it was a strong report across the board. Daly's comments later helped to hammer home the hawkish view on the data. On the flip side, another soft Canadian jobs report has economists raising questions about the wisdom of another rate hike this year. The main focus on the day was on tech and memory names and neoclouds rebounded despite a report saying that Microsoft was cutting down on data center third party rentals. That briefly weighed but the buyers ended up holding the line. Early in the day it looked like there would be a big bounce after Thursday's rout but the gains in memory names were tempered shortly after the open. On the Iran front, there were more positive headlines but not positive enough to really weigh on oil. The effort at diplomacy seems to be priced in now and there will need to be something closer to concrete to As for next week, the earnings drama is far from over as we get CoreWeave on Tuesday and Nebius on Thursday among others. Marcos to Cabinet: Keep prices affordable
articles.desc: PRESIDENT Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Friday directed the Cabinet to keep prices of basic goods affordable, ensure safe and convenient travel, and protect workers’ rights and benefits. The president issued the directive to 10 ad interim officials who took their oath Friday, Presidential Communications O
articles.content: PRESIDENT Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Friday directed the Cabinet to keep prices of basic goods affordable, ensure safe and convenient travel, and protect workers’ rights and benefits. The president issued the directive to 10 ad interim officials who took their oath Friday, Presidential Communications Office Secretary Lino Cayetano said. They are Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida, Public Works Secretary Giovanni Lopez, Labor Secretary Francis Tolentino, Health Secretary Edwin Mercado, Environment Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna, Tourism Secretary Maria Bernardita Mathay, Transportation Secretary Vivencio Dizon, Budget Secretary Kim Robert de Leon, and Philippine Space Agency Director Gay Jane Perez. Marcos urged the officials to prioritize programs that reflect the administration’s commitment to making Christmas more affordable, convenient and meaningful for every Filipino. Recto said the president is focused on helping Filipino families celebrate Christmas with less worry over rising prices and the cost of daily necessities. Recto said the administration will sustain efforts to keep essential goods, particularly food and other basic household needs, affordable and within reach of ordinary Filipinos. Dizon and Lopez pledged to strengthen coordination to ease traffic congestion and improve public transportation, particularly during the holiday rush. Dizon said the president wants commuters to spend less time on the road and save on transportation costs. He said the Department of Transportation will deploy additional buses, trains, and other public transport services to provide commuters with more convenient and accessible travel options. Lopez said the Department of Public Works and Highways will prioritize road repairs and the completion of ongoing projects to reduce traffic delays. The two officials said their agencies will closely coordinate to ensure smoother travel for Filipinos returning to their provinces for Christmas. The administration will also ensure that employers comply with labor laws, including the immediate release of their employees’ holiday wages and other mandatory benefits, the Palace said. These measures aim to protect workers, ease household expenses and allow more Filipino families to enjoy the holiday season, Malacañang said.

articles.title: Microsoft Request Pushes Back IREN's $9.7 Billion Texas AI Data Center Timeline
articles.desc: IREN says a Microsoft-requested network upgrade pushed its $4 billion revenue goal for its Texas AI data center project into 2027.
articles.content: IREN Delays $4B AI Revenue Target Over Microsoft Request Microsoft Request Pushes Back IREN's $9.7 Billion Texas AI Data Center Timeline IREN says its fully contracted, fully funded target of more than $4 billion in annual recurring revenue — originally expected by the end of this year — is now slipping to January 2027, and possibly as late as February. The Australia-based digital infrastructure company, which has pivoted from bitcoin mining toward renewable-energy-powered AI computing, says the delay traces back to a request from its biggest customer: Microsoft. In its fiscal first-quarter results released Thursday, IREN said the revised target reflects what it called a customer-requested change and supplier timing, according to the company's . IREN co-CEO Daniel Roberts identified that customer as Microsoft, telling analysts, “They made a request to reconfigure and upgrade some of the network infrastructure,” according to . The upgrade is reportedly meant to support roughly 200 megawatts of capacity for the latest generation of frontier AI models. The project at the center of the delay is IREN's Childress, Texas campus, built under a $9.7 billion contract with Microsoft and split into four phases, as reported. The first of those four 50-megawatt buildings, known as Horizon 1, went into service for Microsoft during the quarter and received NVIDIA Exemplar status, per the same GlobeNewswire release. Data Center Dynamics has reported that Horizon 1 was the first of four planned 50-megawatt, direct-to-chip liquid-cooled buildings slated for delivery at the site. Satellite Images Raise Questions About the Final Building Not every phase appears to be on the same footing. A satellite flyover on October 21 found that Horizon 4 still lacked backup power generators and cooling equipment, putting its scheduled year-end delivery at risk, according to analysis from Aterio cited by Business Insider. That gap sits alongside a broader pattern the outlet described: research firm Currence has estimated that 30% to 50% of planned data center capacity initially scheduled to come online this year could slip into 2027 or later because of electricity shortages and other construction issues. IREN isn't alone in facing that kind of slippage. Aterio's satellite analysis also found that roughly 140 megawatts of planned capacity at a Nebius project in New Jersey could slip into 2027, Business Insider reported. Bloomberg has characterized the broader landscape bluntly, noting that neocloud companies — firms that rent out AI computing capacity to businesses — are grappling with delays, regulatory snags, and high costs. Despite the timeline slip, IREN's underlying numbers moved in the right direction last quarter. Total quarterly revenue rose 66% sequentially to $228 million, while AI Cloud revenue specifically jumped 182% sequentially to $200 million for the three months ended September 30, according to the GlobeNewswire release. The company's revenue backlog grew 22% sequentially to $20.3 billion, with about two-thirds tied to investment-grade counterparties. IREN's net loss narrowed to $263 million from $684 million in the prior period, CNBC reported. The company's stock had fallen 55% over the past month heading into the earnings report, though shares rose in extended trading once the results came out, per the same CNBC account. IREN wasn't alone in that rough stretch — CoreWeave had plunged 60% over the past month heading into its own earnings report, while Nebius was down 48% over the same period, CNBC noted. The Childress buildout reflects a larger transformation underway at IREN, which built its early business on bitcoin mining before shifting toward AI infrastructure. Data Center Dynamics reported that the firm is winding down its mining operations and diverting cash flow into its AI business. That shift mirrors a wider trend among neocloud operators, who have become an important part of NVIDIA's customer base as the chipmaker extends investments

articles.desc: Maruti expects 30,000 deliveries on Dhanteras; Hyundai targets 16,000, Tata Motors more than 12,000 units
articles.content: Dhanteras sales: top PV makers eye 58,000-plus deliveries | Chennai News - The Times of India Dhanteras sales: top PV makers eye 58,000-plus deliveries Dhanteras sales: top PV makers eye 58,000-plus deliveries Maruti expects to deliver around 30,000 vehicles on Dhanteras Chennai: India’s passenger vehicle market witnessed a sharp festive sales surge on , with Maruti Suzuki, Hyundai Motor India and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles expecting combined deliveries of more than 58,000 vehicles on the auspicious day, while Mahindra & Mahindra reported strong demand, near-zero physical SUV inventory and operations at full capacity. expects to deliver around 30,000 vehicles on Dhanteras, while Hyundai Motor India is targeting 16,000 units, nearly 14% higher than last year. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles expects single-day deliveries to cross 12,000 units. Strong demand extends beyond Dhanteras, with automakers reporting higher retail sales since the start of the festive season, supported by new product launches and sustained customer interest. “From Ganesh Chaturthi on September 14 to November 6, we have already recorded retail sales of over 4 lakh vehicles, compared with 3.46 lakh units during the same period last year,” said Partho Banerjee, senior executive officer, marketing and sales, Maruti Suzuki India. The company has also seen strong demand for the upgraded Brezza and Baleno models. Within two months, Baleno sales crossed 50,000 units and Brezza sales surpassed 70,000 units, with both models carrying substantial pending bookings, Banerjee said. Hyundai Motor India expects deliveries of around 16,000 vehicles across Dhanteras and Diwali, reflecting a nearly 14% increase from the previous year. “Dhanteras and Diwali are among the most auspicious days to bring home a new vehicle, and we are witnessing strong customer demand this year as well,” said Tarun Garg, MD and CEO of Hyundai Motor India. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles has recorded retail growth of more than 20% since Ganesh Chaturthi compared with the corresponding period last year, reflecting sustained demand across markets. “The festive season has delivered strong and sustained demand across markets, with customers nationwide choosing our vehicles to mark the occasion. Newly launched products have added further momentum, strengthening traction across the portfolio,” said Amit Kamat, chief commercial officer of Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles. The company expects the strong momentum to continue, with Diwali muhurat deliveries scheduled through Wednesday. Mahindra & Mahindra, meanwhile, said demand remained strong across its SUV portfolio, with vehicle registrations pointing to robust growth during the festive period. “Based on VAHAN registration data for comparable festive days, starting from Navratri, Mahindra has been the fastest-growing brand over the approximately 25-day period tracked so far,” said Rajesh Jejurikar, ED and CEO, auto and farm sector, Mahindra & Mahindra. The demand surge has tightened supplies. Physical SUV stocks are close to zero across most of Mahindra’s portfolio, with less than eight to nine days of inventory, excluding vehicles in transit. The company is operating at full capacity, with October volumes exceeding previously indicated capacity levels. Mahindra also reported strong demand for its electric SUV portfolio through October and maintained its outlook for mid-to-high-teen SUV volume growth in FY27.
